title: OpenAI’s expensive smart speaker will use moving parts to seem “more alive”
excerpt: OpenAI is venturing into the smart speaker market with a unique product that aims to differentiate…
body:
OpenAI is venturing into the smart speaker market with a unique product that aims to differentiate itself from competitors through innovative design and functionality.

What happened

According to a recent report by Mark Gurman, OpenAI has confirmed that its upcoming smart speaker will feature moving parts, which are intended to give the device a more lifelike presence. This design choice is part of OpenAI’s strategy to create a product that stands out in the crowded smart speaker market. Gurman also highlighted that OpenAI has explicitly stated that this new device is not intended to be a copy of Apple’s offerings, addressing concerns about potential comparisons to existing products from the tech giant.

Why it matters

The introduction of a smart speaker by OpenAI could signify a significant shift in the market, particularly as the company is known for its advancements in artificial intelligence. By incorporating moving parts, OpenAI aims to enhance user interaction, making the speaker feel more engaging and responsive. This could redefine user expectations for smart devices, pushing competitors to innovate further in terms of design and functionality.

Moreover, the clarification that OpenAI’s product is not an imitation of Apple’s designs is crucial for positioning in the marketplace. As tech companies often face scrutiny regarding originality, OpenAI’s proactive stance may help it carve out a distinct identity in the smart speaker segment. The emphasis on creating a product that feels “more alive” could resonate with consumers seeking a more interactive and personalized experience in their smart home devices.

As the smart speaker landscape continues to evolve, OpenAI’s entry with a focus on unique design elements could set new trends and inspire other companies to explore innovative features that enhance user engagement. The potential for moving parts to create a more dynamic interaction could lead to a new wave of smart devices that prioritize not just functionality but also user experience.

Source: arstechnica.com.
